items.html:
One correctness issue; derivative scaling itself is correct.

  • New artificial overflow for outgoing waves at fields.rs:165-170. For l=40, m=0, k=1e-4, position [0,0,1], the new scale gives k'=1, r'=1e-4. Although h₄₀(1e-4) ≈ 10²²³ is representable, scaled_radial divides it by (r')⁴⁰=10⁻¹⁶⁰, producing approximately 10³⁸³. Subsequent multiplication by the tiny solid harmonic cannot recover the finite field. The previous coordinates have r=1 and avoid this overflow; the physical N field and first derivatives remain representable. This also contradicts the revised documentation’s implication that only unrepresentable dimensionless Bessel values fail. Use position-based scaling for outgoing waves; the inverse-wavenumber floor serves the regular origin series.

  • The mathematical transformation and chain factors are correct. Solid harmonics scale as S(r/s)=s⁻ˡS(r), gradients as s⁻⁽ˡ⁻¹⁾, and c'=sˡc, so both M and N values are invariant. Holding s fixed gives ∂k F = s ∂k' F and ∂r F = s⁻¹ ∂r' F. This remains valid even where the chosen max scale changes; its derivatives need not be included.

  • The cache-key change is necessary and correct: scaled solid harmonics now depend on the wavenumber.

Source/math review only; no tests, builds, or edits.
